clue.text: Emergency treatment gets tree settled

parts.note: a fir is a common conifer
settled in one's ways, sober and sedate

explanation.surface: Someone hurt by a falling tree gets treated once things calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the immediate care given to an injured person before a doctor or ambulance arrives.

clue.text: See 4
Change of level of racket

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slope joining a higher surface to a lower one
second meaning: British slang for a swindle or fraudulent scheme

explanation.surface: A change in the noise level of a din.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a ramp is a swindle, the sense that matches racket as a crooked scheme rather than a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an inclined slope between two heights and, informally in Britain, a dishonest money-making trick.

clue.text: Seat lost on purpose, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, so the phrase before it is matched by pronunciation only

parts.note: a match deliberately lost is said to have been thrown

explanation.surface: A political seat deliberately given away in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is the ceremonial chair of a monarch, a particular kind of seat.

clue.text: World bank is, in lofty manner, anti-trade union movement

indicators.note: a movement shifts things about, so the preceding letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, part of the raw material
the rest of the raw material, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A haughty global bank is accused of backing a campaign against organised labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anti-trade union movement' reads as a political campaign, but 'movement' is the anagram signal and every letter before it from 'lofty' onwards is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The IMF is a global financial institution lending to member countries, fairly described as a bank serving the whole world.

clue.text: Effect when one member passed bill

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament
a parliamentary bill that has been passed becomes law under this name

explanation.surface: A lone MP manages to get legislation through and it makes a difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the influence or result something has, a close synonym of effect as a noun.

clue.text: See 4
Some score it a tedious affair, a turn-up for loops, etc

indicators.note: in a down clue a turn-up flips the column so the string reads from the bottom upwards
only some of the following word is wanted, here its opening part

parts.note: the opening two letters of the word
taken as written
taken as written
something tedious is a bore
taken as written, the article before 'turn-up'

explanation.surface: Some people rate a stunt show dull, yet it surprises them with its loops.
explanation.walkthrough: The string is built in clue order and then read upwards. 'A turn-up for' also reads as 'a surprise', disguising the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobatics are the stunts flown by aircraft, of which loops, rolls and spins are typical examples.

clue.text: Coming across as model to wild party-goer on wrong note

parts.note: the Model T Ford

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: someone who goes to raves or lives wildly
a note or notice is a sign

explanation.surface: A fashion model at a wild party is heard singing off-key.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford gives the single letter. 'On' just places the last piece after the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Traversing means crossing from one side to the other, the same action as coming across.

clue.text: The top line is miners take time — little time — to strike gold

parts.note: the National Union of Mineworkers
an era is a period of time
T is the abbreviation for time
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline: striking miners are taking their time to hit gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers, famous for its strikes. 'The top line' is the definition, not a headline.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction the number written above the bar is called the numerator, literally its upper line.

clue.text: Sport causing disturbance — eating meat, nothing more

indicators.note: something eating takes food inside itself, so one string swallows the other

parts.note: civil disorder in the streets
meat is animal flesh
zero looks like the letter

explanation.surface: A street fight breaks out over meat while people go hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: The meat and nothing go in after the first two letters of the disturbance; 'more' just adds the nothing to the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Target shooting with a rifle is an organised competitive sport, including at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Major opera?

parts.note: surface reading: a big, important work of opera
setter's reading: the wife of John Major, Prime Minister in 1991, shares her first name with a Bellini opera

explanation.walkthrough: John Major was British Prime Minister when this was set; his wife's first name is also the title of Bellini's opera about a druid priestess.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's tragic opera bears this title, and Mrs Major bore the same name, so it is both an opera and a Major.

clue.text: Not making anything of a blueprint for reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

parts.note: all twelve letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A political reform plan turns out to achieve nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that is unprofitable makes no money, which is what not making anything means here.

clue.text: Formula for going round one checked for duration with versatility in computing

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one string wraps the other
something going is leaving, so the named word departs from the longer one

parts.note: taken as written
the word to be taken out
a race or task checked with a stopwatch is timed
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A racing formula is checked for timing on a computer that does everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formula' looks like motor racing, and 'one checked for duration' reads as a timed lap; the word 'for' is both surface glue and the piece that leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Multimedia computing combines text, sound, pictures and video, which is a kind of versatility.

clue.text: Sulk by Fitzgerald, Reagan leading her a dance

parts.note: to be in a pet is to be in a sulk
Ronald Reagan, US President
Ella Fitzgerald, jazz singer

explanation.surface: A sulking Ella Fitzgerald being led round the floor by Ronald Reagan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' points back to Ella, so Ron comes first, leading her. Petronella is a Scottish country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Petronella is a traditional Scottish country dance, so it is one example of a dance.

clue.text: American edition, somewhat imperfect?

parts.note: abbreviation for the United States
the usual abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A US printing of a book that contains some errors.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a used item is secondhand and so slightly worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used is secondhand and has some wear, so it is no longer in perfect condition.

clue.text: Pre-privatisation payments for animal that's endangered at two points

parts.note: the water vole, often called a water rat
two compass points, east and south; the water vole is itself endangered

explanation.surface: Charges levied to protect a threatened riverbank creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Before English water was privatised in 1989, households paid water rates to the local authority. The compass points are E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Water rates were the household charges for water supply in Britain, paid before the industry was sold off.

clue.text: Square stones connected with eastern country

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's tool
hailstones fall as hail
and joins one thing with another

explanation.surface: A town square paved with stones in an Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand is a nation in South-East Asia, so it is an eastern country.

clue.text: Set fire to window as illumination for procession?

parts.note: to torch a building is to set it alight
a light is a pane or window

explanation.surface: An arsonist sets a window ablaze, lighting up a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Torchlight is the light given by flaming torches, as carried in a nighttime parade.

clue.text: Look what verse can do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look over quickly
second meaning: a line of verse does this when its metre is regular

explanation.surface: An invitation to see what poetry is capable of.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to glance over something quickly and, of poetry, to fit a regular metrical pattern.

clue.text: Film produced by a gypsy choir

indicators.note: the letters are produced by the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: A movie made by a choir of travelling singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller, a famous film.

clue.text: Two residences in one?

parts.note: surface reading: a building that combines two homes
setter's reading: two words for a dwelling joined into one name

explanation.walkthrough: The Mansion House is the official London residence of the Lord Mayor of the City of London, and its name is two words for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The building is itself one residence, yet its name is made of two words that each mean a home.

clue.text: Fish with a tail?

parts.note: a common sea fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish that has a tail, as fish do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail' looks like part of the fish, but it is the definition: the Italian word means tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a piece of music, from the Italian for tail.

clue.text: Bird talk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a talking bird, such as a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small songbird family and also means relaxed conversation.

clue.text: Big mouth of model talking!
Unwilling to keep worrying Colin about minimum wear

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one string goes within the other

parts.note: an old spelling of loath

indicators.note: worrying at something shakes it about, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the name as written

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to keep fretting over Colin, who wears very little.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single strip of fabric round the hips, about as little clothing as one can wear.

clue.text: Prizes in the direction of an article

parts.note: the indefinite article
the suffix meaning in the direction of, as in homewards

explanation.surface: Prizes sent off to a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocks are read in reverse clue order: the article comes first and the suffix follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Awards are honours or prizes given for achievement, so the plural noun matches prizes.

clue.text: Soldier retreating — no wild talk — it could be blissful

indicators.note: a retreating soldier goes backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: an American soldier
taken as written
a wild, angry speech

explanation.surface: A soldier pulls back and refuses to rant, perhaps happily.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Thomas Gray's line 'where ignorance is bliss, 'tis folly to be wise'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that not knowing can bring happiness, so being uninformed may well be blissful.
